anomalies.observed: The schematic text carries two different values for R48 next to Q9 (AO3401A PMOS): one block reads "+3V3 10K R48" and a second block reads "Q9 AO3401A ... R48 210K". The drawing does not say which is correct.
anomalies.expected: R48 is a single gate pull-up on the switched +3V3 PMOS, consistent with the other PMOS gate pull-ups in the same section (R58, R63, R47 and R62 are all 10K). A 10K value would be expected, and a 210K value would leave the gate weakly pulled up.

evidence.quote: "+3V3 10K R48" (Power Control / Serial area text block, sheet cm4-robot, page 1)
"JP8 1 2 +5V Q9 AO3401A 1 3 R48 210K" (sheet cm4-robot, page 1, second text layer)

anomalies.impact: If R48 is 210K, the Q9 gate turns off slowly and the switched 3.3V rail may power up with a delay or at an unintended threshold. If the text is only a duplicate layer, there is no functional impact.

anomalies.observed: The buck converter U12 (FB on pin 4, EN on pin 1) has its feedback divider labeled R16 205k and R17 1.8M. The ratio of about 8.8 would set the output near 12V with a 1.23V reference, not +5V as the net label indicates.
anomalies.expected: The feedback divider for the +5V output should give about 5V, which for a 1.23V reference means a top/bottom ratio near 3. A 1.8M top resistor with a 205k bottom resistor does not match a +5V rail.

evidence.quote: "C19 22pF 50V R16 205k" and "C22 22pF 50V 1.8M R17" (sheet cm4-robot, page 1, Power section)
"+5V EN 4 FB 3 VIN 5 GND 2 SW 1 U12" (sheet cm4-robot, page 1)

anomalies.impact: If the divider really is 205k/1.8M, the +5V rail would regulate far above 5V, which would overvoltage the 5V-powered loads (CM4, LEDs, USB) and could damage them. The reference designator/value mapping in the extracted text is ambiguous, so this may be a text-extraction artifact.

parsed.summary: The schematic text is hard to map to pins reliably, but two passive values look inconsistent with their roles: R48 appears as both 10K and 210K as a PMOS gate pull-up, and the +5V buck feedback divider (R16 205k / R17 1.8M) would set about 12V rather than 5V. Both findings are low confidence because of the ambiguous text layout.
